audit.why: Mirror reuse: audits/top/rumble__trundle.json already audited this lane from Rumble's side and scored the difficulty read as correct — Rumble owns levels 2-3, the lane is even 4-6, Trundle takes over late. Both charts on disk are identical (Skill/Rumble/Rumble/Skill/Skill/Rumble/Rumble), so I changed no stage rather than introduce a disagreement mirror-fix would have to undo.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0] claims 'Rumble's Flamespitter hits max rank' at levels 2-3, and early repeats 'Flamespitter hitting max early rank' at level 3. A rank-2 ability is not max rank. spikes[2] also spells his item 'Liandy's Torment'.
audit.why: The spike markers are the part players read to plan a back timing; naming a rank that cannot exist at level 3 undermines the rest of the card.
audit.corrected: Recast around what actually changes: the cone burns for 3 seconds, Danger Zone at 50% Heat empowers it, and Scrap Shield is a flat 6-second cooldown. Item name corrected to Liandry's Torment. The Equalizer's 130s rank-1 cooldown added.

audit.whatIsWrong: Electro Harpoon is never mentioned once in the entire matchup, in either layer. It is his 850-range poke, he carries two charges on a 0.5s cooldown, and it REDUCES MAGIC RESIST on hit — while the same matchup tells you to solve the lane by buying magic resist. The mirror's finding that Rumble has no dash against Pillar of Ice's terrain was also absent from this side.
audit.why: Point 4 is the key point, and this is the one ability that changes what the itemization advice is worth. MR still helps, but he is shredding it back every harpoon, so the stacking has to go further than 'one Spirit Visage'.
audit.corrected: Electro Harpoon named with its range, charge count and MR reduction in whys[1], wants.you[2], wants.foe[0] and mid; Pillar of Ice stated as a wall he must walk around, since he has no dash — matching the mirror.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Bait Scrap Shield' appeared three times with no indication of how long the bait buys you.
audit.why: Scrap Shield is a flat 6 seconds and Chomp is a flat 3.5 — so a baited shield is one clean bite and an auto reset, not a free all-in. That single number changes how much a player commits.
audit.corrected: The 6s figure written into wants.you[0], whys[2], whys[3], early and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Pillar disrupts any Equalizer line of fire' asserts that Pillar of Ice blocks or breaks The Equalizer.
audit.why: Riot's Equalizer text describes rockets creating a wall of flames at up to 1750 range; nothing available here says impassable terrain interrupts it. The verified version is about foot traffic, not the cast.
audit.corrected: Rewritten as Pillar cutting the walking path into and out of the flame wall, which follows directly from Pillar being impassable terrain and Rumble having no dash.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid invented a number: 'a target sitting on 60+ bonus MR mid-fight'.
audit.why: Subjugate's text gives a percent steal that doubles over 4 seconds, with no absolute figure. The mirror hit the same problem from the other side (it found '40% for 8 seconds' and 'a third' in the same matchup) and resolved it the same way.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the mechanic Riot states — percent of health, armour and MR on cast, doubling over the next 4 seconds — and the resulting instruction to cast on his commit rather than as a finisher.

edits.before: Rumble's Flamespitter hits max rank and his overheat bar starts mattering — he chunks you with sustained AP damage before you can get Frozen Domain running underneath him.
edits.after: Flamespitter (10s at rank 1) burns a cone for 3 seconds and Danger Zone at 50% Heat empowers it — he chunks you well before Frozen Domain is running underneath him.

edits.before: Trinity Force's Spellblade procs on every Chomp — this is your duel-power peak and the window to solo him repeatedly before his Liandy's Torment fully comes online.
edits.after: Trinity Force's Spellblade procs on every Chomp — this is your duel-power peak and the window to solo him before Liandry's Torment fully comes online.

edits.before: Bait Scrap Shield before you commit Q — bite him the instant his W is on cooldown and the trade pattern is yours
edits.after: Bait Scrap Shield first — it is only 6s, so bite inside that gap and reset Chomp off the auto every 3.5s

edits.before: Build Spirit Visage or Mercury Treads early to reduce Flamespitter's DoT so you can outlast his heat bar and punish him when he overheats
edits.after: Build MR early and stack further than feels necessary — Electro Harpoon reduces your magic resist on hit and he holds two charges

edits.before: Run Flamespitter through your W zone to negate your movement speed bonus and DoT you out of the trade before Chomp can decide it
edits.after: Hold Flamespitter's cone over your W zone and stack Electro Harpoon slows so the DoT settles the trade before Chomp can

edits.before: Land Equalizer across your likely retreat path to zone you off the wave and burn your health before a second engage
edits.after: Land The Equalizer (130s at rank 1) across your retreat path to zone you off the wave and burn you before a second engage

edits.before: Flamespitter comes online at level 2 and Rumble runs it through your feet before Frozen Domain is maxed enough to offset it — the sustained AP DoT beats your short-trade tools at this stage.
edits.after: Flamespitter comes online at 2 and burns in a cone for 3 seconds, and Electro Harpoon chips from 850 range while shredding your MR — the DoT beats your short-trade tools here.

edits.before: Flamespitter now has an additional rank and Scrap Shield is reliably absorbing your engage attempt — he out-DPSes you in any trade that runs past your initial Chomp hit.
edits.after: Flamespitter gains a rank and Scrap Shield (6s flat) absorbs your engage — he out-damages you in any trade past the first Chomp, so bite only inside the shield gap.

edits.before: Neither Flamespitter's DoT nor Frozen Domain's sustained bonuses cleanly dominate — the advantage swings with overheat timing, Scrap Shield cooldown, and how well you keep the ice zone under your feet.
edits.after: Neither Flamespitter's DoT nor Frozen Domain's sustained bonuses cleanly dominate — the advantage swings with Danger Zone timing at 50% Heat, Scrap Shield's flat 6-second cooldown, and where you keep the ice.

edits.before: Two items of MR — Spirit Visage or Force of Nature — absorbs Flamespitter completely, and Subjugate resist-steal at full build is overwhelming: you win every extended side-lane fight with Subjugate available and outlast him without it.
edits.after: Two items of MR — Spirit Visage or Force of Nature — blunt Flamespitter, and Spirit Visage compounds with Frozen Domain, which increases healing from every source. Subjugate's theft doubles over 4 seconds, so cast it on his commit, never to finish.

edits.before: Level 1 is deceptively neutral: Q Chomp bites Rumble for solid flat damage and steals a chunk of his AD, but he has no abilities yet so neither of you has a defined pattern. Respect that and use the bite on every step-up attempt he makes to last-hit, banking tiny HP leads without overcommitting. At level 2 Rumble gains Flamespitter and the matchup shifts against you — his sustained fire DoT runs under your early Chomp and the W zone does not yet offset it, so he wins trades that extend past two seconds. Level 3 is the low point: Flamespitter hitting max early rank plus Scrap Shield absorbing your engage attempt means he can simply out-damage your healing in a committed fight. Play around wave position, not aggression. Never trade into Scrap Shield; let him waste it on a shield bait before you step forward.
edits.after: Level 1 is deceptively neutral: Chomp bites Rumble for solid flat damage and saps his AD, but he has no abilities yet so neither of you has a defined pattern. Use the bite on every step-up he makes to last-hit, banking tiny HP leads without overcommitting. At level 2 Rumble gains Flamespitter and the matchup shifts against you — the cone burns for 3 seconds and runs under your early Chomp, so he wins any trade that extends past two seconds. Level 3 is the low point: a second rank of Flamespitter plus Scrap Shield, which is a flat 6-second cooldown, means he out-damages your healing in a committed fight. Note what he lacks, though: Rumble has no dash, so Pillar of Ice (21s at rank 1) is a wall he has to walk around. Play wave position, not aggression, and never trade into a fresh Scrap Shield.

edits.before: The window flips at level 6. Subjugate into a mid-game Rumble drains his MR and piles it onto you — the same Flamespitter that was melting you now hits a target sitting on 60+ bonus MR mid-fight. Use R immediately when he commits, not as a finisher, so the resist-steal pays across the entire duration of the trade. Between 4-6 the lane is a skill check: drop W under yourself before every trade so the movement speed eats his kiting and the healing patches his DoT ticks, and use Pillar behind him to cut off escape once you close the gap. Track his heat bar — if he overheats trying to out-damage your W healing, his next several autos are empowered but his Q goes quiet, and that is the cleanest duel window you will get before level 6.
edits.after: The window flips at level 6. Subjugate takes a percent of his health, armour and magic resist and stacks it on you, and the theft doubles over the next 4 seconds — so cast it the moment he commits, not as a finisher. Keep in mind that Electro Harpoon reduces magic resist on every hit and he carries two charges, so what you steal is being chipped back all fight. Between 4-6 the lane is a skill check: drop W under yourself before every trade so the move speed eats his kiting and the healing patches his DoT ticks, and put Pillar of Ice behind him once you have closed, because he has no dash to cross it. Track his Heat — at 100% he Overheats, gaining attack speed and empowered autos but unable to cast for a few seconds, and that is the cleanest duel window you get before level 6.

edits.before: Late game this becomes a clean Trundle carry threat. Your Trinity Force plus Spirit Visage makes you nearly unkillable to Rumble's kit in a 1v1 — Flamespitter's DoT is healed back by W and passive King's Tribute procs off every minion, and Subjugate strips whatever MR stacking he builds into. Splitpush with Frozen Domain active and force him to match you, or let him rotate and take the structure. In teamfights, Subjugate goes onto their tankiest frontliner and Pillar disrupts any Equalizer line of fire — do not let him stand still in his R zone unchallenged. The only real danger at this stage is walking into a surprise R with your Subjugate already spent, so track it the same way he tracks your cooldowns early.
edits.after: Late game this becomes a clean Trundle carry threat. Trinity Force plus Spirit Visage makes you nearly unkillable to Rumble's kit in a 1v1 — Flamespitter's DoT is healed back inside Frozen Domain, which increases healing from every source, King's Tribute procs off every dying minion, and Subjugate strips whatever resists he stacks into. Splitpush with Frozen Domain active and force him to match you, or let him rotate and take the structure. In teamfights Subjugate goes onto their tankiest frontliner, and Pillar of Ice cuts the walking path into and out of his flame wall, since he has no dash. The real danger at this stage is walking into a surprise Equalizer with your Subjugate already spent.

edits.before: - Rumble Scrap Shield: matchup-defining — Bait it, then commit. Track it before every engage. - Rumble The Equalizer: A long line of fire that zones and chunks — his teamfight tool. Dodge or sidestep it.
edits.after: - Scrap Shield (W): a flat 6s. Bait it, then bite — that gap is one Chomp and an auto reset, not a free all-in. - The Equalizer (R): 130/105/80s. He has no dash, so Pillar of Ice decides who walks out of the flames.

edits.before: Pillar closes the kit — use it behind Rumble to deny disengage, or between you and Scrap Shield to break his pattern.
edits.after: Pillar of Ice closes your kit and Rumble has no dash to cross it — drop it behind him once Scrap Shield's 6 seconds are spent.

edits.before: Q ranks raise the bite damage and the AD steal. Keep trading in W; if Rumble stands in your domain trading evenly, he is losing.
edits.after: Chomp ranks up while his Heat management decides trades. Bite inside Frozen Domain and step out of the cone rather than tanking it.

edits.before: Subjugate online — the 1v1 is yours into almost anyone the moment Rumble commits. R early in the all-in so the drained resists count for the whole fight.
edits.after: Subjugate online — the steal doubles over 4 seconds, so cast it as Rumble commits rather than to finish, and the whole trade is fought on his resists.

edits.before: Track Rumble's Scrap Shield: Bait it, then commit. When it is down — Bite + duel him.
edits.after: Scrap Shield is a flat 6s: bait it, then bite. Electro Harpoon shreds the MR you build.

notes: MIRROR CONFLICT worth the user's attention: audits/top/rumble__trundle.json states in its point-2 rationale that 'Trundle takes over at two items', but both champions' charts on disk score first item AND 2+ items for Rumble, and that mirror proposal contains no chart edit. Trundle's own prose here (spikes[2], spikes[3], whys[5], whys[6], late) also says Trundle wins those stages. I left both charts untouched so the two sides stay identical — flipping only my side would just be reverted by mirror-fix.js. See questionsForUser. Kit-flag misfires noted and not written: Scrap Shield carries derived flags for 'knockup' and 'terrain' that Riot's description does not support (it is a shield plus a burst of speed), and Flamespitter carries no cooldown-relevant flag beyond 'zone'. All four packet suspectNames for this matchup are false positives — 'Run Flamespitter', 'Use Scrap Shield', 'Land Equalizer' and "Frozen Domain's" are all correct names with a verb in front.
